priorPassage.text:
| Component | Current role | Current source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Work Lifecycle Engine / Work Driver | Domain-agnostic work-unit lifecycle, status board, claim/return, human gates. Does not own stage or sequencing (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)): execution and progress authority for a case on the ledger is the Workflow case, and Work keeps the status lifecycle, claim/return, slots, settlement and the `workflowRunId` pointer; the coding step FSM stays the authority for coding items until the coding cutover. Owns worker slots (`OccupancyPort`), and fail-safe claim settlement (`fgos return --to blocked`). | [../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md](../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md) |
| Workflow (guide + case; `src/workflow/**`) | Component Workflow with two entities, guide and case (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), partially supersedes 0048 §2 and 0049 §4; behaviour per [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md), implementation follows its plan). Human review gates. A consumer of Git's Land and Sync; owns no git mutation of its own. Single authority for the guide schema and its pinned snapshot per case; the case ledger (approved frame, reservations, route/deviation events, gate answers bound to subject digests, receipts, milestone projection, close); admission (is a proposed activity lawful now, against a closed catalog of machine checks); the worktree binding record (keyed by worktree root identity, with a generation) and the frame counters. Implements the AdmissionPort that Execution Core declares; imports flow Workflow → Execution Core only. Chooses no order: the agent proposes, the case admits and records; the Playbook proposer proposes through admission like any agent. Admission predicates, projection and the port implementation sit at infra or lower; the Playbook proposer at use-case. The ledger stays the JSONL under `advance`, hardened in place (fsync before release, reader fails closed); not an Event Store consumer in this cutover (owner 2026-10-19). Consumer of Execution Core and Git. Never owns who/model/persona, verify execution, locks, writer identity, merge or Work status. | [../specs/workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md), [../specs/runner.md](../specs/runner.md) |
| Execution Core (Unit, Unit run, `bind()`, Pattern cộng tác, cửa `fgos run`, posture) | Single authority for "ai làm / model / persona / cơ chế" (`src/runner/execution/bind.mjs`), single run door for new work (`fgos run` via `src/runner/execution/run.mjs`, herdr pane default, cli fallback), OS confinement posture for both herdr and cli, verifiable mutating gate. Strictly forbids L3 Work lifecycle dependencies (`src/state/**`). Owns the AdmissionPort interface (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)) (resolve the target worktree's binding, admit, settle), never the admission decision; every `runUnit` caller with writes (the run door, the Playbook proposer and the Work paths running today) injects Workflow's real implementation from the day it lands, and the port accepts an `advance` hold the caller already has. `runUnit` refuses a mutating Unit with no port, and a standalone write passes only on an affirmative `unbound`. The door resolves the caller's authority context conjunctively after pattern resolution and before `bind()`; the port stays present at the mutating gate, which re-checks subject-bound consent at effect; the door sets the case context in the worker's launch env and strips any inherited one. A nested writing dispatch from a confined worker is refused by name (owner 2026-10-19). | [../specs/runner.md](../specs/runner.md) |
| Collaboration Patterns (Execution Core) | Domain-neutral small collaboration loops (`solo`, `reviewed`, `panel`) and presets (`consult`, `research-fan-out`, `rfc`). Replaces retired coordination engine. | [../specs/runner.md](../specs/runner.md) |
| Herdr (Transport chính + Bề mặt quan sát) | Transport mặc định cho out-of-process runs, pane execution liveness, plugin `herdr-dashboard/` (TUI trong pane herdr + pick/pane supervisor; herdr nạp qua `herdr-plugin.toml`). | [../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md](../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md) |
| fgos Gateway | Tiến trình detached duy nhất phục vụ REST API (`/v1`, hợp đồng CTR010), MCP `search`/`execute` trên cùng cổng, và bundle web dashboard nhúng sẵn (`apps/fgos-gateway/`: `gateway.rs`, `mcp.rs`, `cf_access.rs`, `remote_invocation.rs`, `web/`). Vòng đời duy nhất qua `fgos gateway start\|status\|stop`; không phải một phần của herdr và không phải "herdr-gateway" (tên đó chỉ repo tham chiếu ngoài). Dùng chung với `herdr-dashboard` lớp adapter CLI fgos tại `packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust` (`fgos.rs`, `settings.rs`, trait `WorkItemSource`). | [../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md](../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md) |
| Dispatch Transport & Confinement | Machine backend registry, isolation confinement (`bwrap` v1 driver, attestation storage, fail-closed probes), executor adapters; the `bwrap` driver calls the credential renewal module at provisioning (`copyCredentialFiles`, the write-back marker) and removing a private home (`confinement/cleanup.mjs`) calls it again for write-back (dependency confinement → provider capacity, for the account lock only). | [../specs/confinement-authority.md](../specs/confinement-authority.md) |
| Run Result Evaluator | Evidence/confidence boundary for assignment run results. | [../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md](../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md) |
| Domain Components And Extension Layer | Domain-specific behavior, workflows, skills, task specs, doctrine. L2 prose no longer picks executors or mechanisms (lớp matching L2 cũ đã thu hồi per 0048); thin driver `fgos-run` delegates directly to Workflow runner and P1 Execution Core. | [../../domains/](../../domains/), [../architect/domainization/](../architect/domainization/) |
| Host And Surface Layer | CLI, fgos Gateway (REST/MCP/web), `herdr-dashboard` plugin and other Herdr surfaces into platform engines. | Host invocation and gateway docs |
| Packaging-Distribution | Runtime packaging, install, activation, setup/doctor readiness. | [packaging-distribution/README.md](packaging-distribution/README.md) |
| Knowledge, Learning, And Documentation Registry | Retrospective learning, doc registry, end-user docs index, trace/evolve signals. | Knowledge and docs registry docs |
| Observe (Metrics & Friction) | Measurement and friction tracking across substrate entities (cases, runs, sessions, friction, snapshots). Owned in Rust (`packages/observe/rust`), native routing. | [../specs/observe.md](../specs/observe.md) |
| Convention (Executable Names & Placement) | Platform-core authority for deterministic artifact names, repository-relative placement, path classification, and conformance checking. Implemented; owns no state and depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. | [convention/spec.md](convention/spec.md) |
| Session Identity (Writer Identity) | Foundation authority for "who is the writer of this process" (`{id, source}`). One implementation, the Rust crate `fgos-session-identity` (`packages/session-identity/rust`, native verb `fgos identity`); Observe calls it in process, Node through the facade `src/util/session-identity.mjs`. Also mints the writer id of an attempt (`att-<attemptId>`, route `fgos internal identity mint-attempt`) and carries the launcher's env scrub the gate applies. Owns no state and depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`; Observe depends on it; the run supervisor's controller half calls the mint. Grants no lock or claim authority. | [session-identity/spec.md](session-identity/spec.md) |
| Terminal-control (L2) | Foundation component for "which pane does this key run in" on a terminal multiplexer, usable without a run. Rust crate `fgos-terminal-control` (`packages/terminal-control/rust`) with a key-addressed upper port and a driver port with declared capabilities (herdr first; Windows declares none). Writes only the allocation record; closes only panes it allocated, never a tab; Node reaches it through the internal route `fgos internal terminal-control`, no user verb. Dependency one way: run supervisor → Terminal-control (the supervisor holds the key, the attempt id, never a pane). Node migration done; setup adds the `terminal` config section and `<stateRoot>/terminal`, doctor runs `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations`. | [terminal-control/spec.md](terminal-control/spec.md) |
| Process Facts & Control (L0) | Single authority for "is this process tuple `{host, bootId, pidNs, pid, startTime}` alive, dead or unknown" (`judge`, one shared vector file for Rust and Node), for signalling a process by identity (`pidfd` on Linux, never a bare pid), for spawning with an explicit fd mapping, and for the domain primitives `domain_is_empty`/`domain_kill_all` the predecessor rule of holder-lock needs. Never spawns to read facts, never kills by bare pid, never reads mtime, knows no run, lock or pane. Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), one driver per OS; the Node leaf `src/runner/dispatch/process-identity.mjs` reads the same vectors, and reconcile imports only `facts`. The gate primitives (subreaper, PDEATHSIG, PID namespace, tty) stay with the run supervisor; the containment port lives in this crate (row below). Depends only on the OS. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md) |
| Holder-lock (L1) | Single authority for "who holds which resource", as the kernel sees it: kernel locks on open file descriptions behind one OS-neutral port (`acquire`, `release`, `run_borrowed`, `probe`, `holders`, `guarantee`), the lock registry (`packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json`: every lock's kind, scope, rank, path, legacy shape and fence), lock order inside one `LockScope`, the description rules, the predecessor-domain rule, the single state-root resolution and the cutover fences. Never reads writer identity, never takes a lock from a live holder, never derives a decision from a pid, TTL or mtime. Rust crate `fgos-holder-lock` (`packages/holder-lock/rust`) plus the internal routes `fgos internal lock-fd|state-root|quiesce-scan|lock-borrow-vectors`; Node only through the facade `src/holder-lock/`, which never exposes an fd. Depends on Process Facts & Control and the kernel. Owns the cold locks (gateway, runner, sessions, advance, reconcile, recovery, full-suite, provider account/state, dispatch cwd) and the main checkout mutex (one door `withMainCheckout`, git children and the pre-commit hook borrow the lock through the description, no pid or TTL), the merge slot and `worktree-admin`; `fgos lock fence` is the one door for a hung live holder. `advance` follows Shape C (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), owner 2026-10-19, [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)): a conductor case holds it for one reserve or one release/settle; the Playbook proposer holds it for the life of its loop, so its holder is the proposer's liveness, as today; a dispatch naming a live playbook case from inside its own Unit is refused by name. `answer` never appends directly: it writes the gate-answer file and tries `advance` once. The worktree binding is one exclusively created file per worktree, not a registry row. No new lock row; rank stays 80; no re-rank for an Event Store cutover. It does not own the state store's hot mutex (`state`, `porting-events`: `withStateTx` in `src/state/hot-lock.mjs`, which replaced `events.lock`, `claims.lock` and `porting/events.lock`): the state store owns that mechanism, a temporary one until the store moves to Rust, and takes only its cleanup lock and the fences from this component. The main door's `.fgos` checkpoint is a detachable adapter, so the lock core knows nothing of the event log. | [holder-lock/spec.md](holder-lock/spec.md) |
| Containment port (L0) | Single authority for "which processes belong to this attempt, and are there any left": an OS-neutral process domain per attempt (`create`, `spawn_in`, `is_empty`, `kill_all`, `guarantee`) with one driver per OS (`bwrap-pidns` and `linux-pgroup` on Linux, `windows-job`, `macos-tree`), each reporting a guarantee level (`kernel` or `best-effort`) and its named escapes. Knows no attempt beyond the id that names a domain, and no envelope, lock or pane. Module `containment` of the Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), contract `packages/process/contracts/containment.port.v1.json`; depends only on the OS. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md#10-containment-port) |
| Git (foundation) | Single authority for repository facts, typed Git operations and their recovery WAL: every fgOS mutation of local objects, refs, index, worktrees and worktree registration, the local side of fetch and push, and operation recovery, through typed ports (Inspect, Refs, Worktree, ScopedCommit, Sync, Land, SafeRestore, RepositoryConfig, Remote, Recovery, Publication); no public `git(args)` port. Its Publication port is the only door to `refs/fgos/*`, and Event Store is the only production writer of event refs through it. Owns no business approval, Work lifecycle, event semantics or lock mechanism. Consumers: Workflow, Execution Core, Work, Event Store, setup. Depends on Holder-lock, Process Facts & Control and Session Identity; imports no consumer. Rust crate `fgos-git` (`packages/git/rust`, planned); Node reaches it only through the one combined N-API addon that also links `fgos-event-store`. Not implemented: today's Node git writers stay until the Git plan replaces them in one release per caller family. | [git/spec.md](git/spec.md) |
| Event Store | Signed design D-ADR0055; implementation not started. Owns event durability after `fsync`, sealing immutable git objects on per-machine `refs/fgos/events/<machine-id>`, publication/sync and deterministic union reads. One Rust core with a thin Node facade; consumer reducers and rebuildable views remain with consumers, claims/leases remain runtime state. Uses Process and Holder-lock; planned `event-seal` rank 58 and `event-append` rank 70 are specified, not yet registered or implemented. Work is the first consumer; porting, observe and decisions follow. Acceptance requires spec §23 gates; no current state-store ownership transfer is claimed. | [event-store/spec.md](event-store/spec.md) |
| Run Supervisor (L4) | One Rust process per attempt that owns the attempt after the controller handed it over: holds the attempt lock and the cwd lease, creates the containment domain, starts the launch gate, watches the soft deadline and idle, publishes the receipt and the per-step receipts, runs the post-receipt steps and owns the adopt door (`fgos internal adopt`, one door for resume, recover, scan and home cleanup). A supervisor that dies leaves the agent running; adopt settles it. Never knows a pane or a terminal, never picks a provider or retries, never judges the work (Run Result Evaluator inside the Node `settle-attempt` step). Crate `fgos-run-supervisor` (`packages/run-supervisor/rust`), routes `fgos internal supervise\|gate\|adopt\|attempt-step` (protocol 1, not in help), Node client and steps in `src/run-supervisor/`. Depends on Containment port, Process Facts & Control, Holder-lock and agent-protocol. Two launch modes: `direct` (headless process) and `terminal` (an agent in a terminal-control pane, addressed by the attempt id; the supervisor listens on an attempt socket, drives the pane through the agent protocol and ends with a `release-slot` step). Depends also on Terminal-control (in process, by key). | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md) |
| Launch gate (L4, part of the run supervisor) | The process root of the agent inside the containment domain (pid 1 of a fresh PID namespace on Linux): owns the agent's IO (capture files, stdin; in `terminal` mode the pane's tty, with the agent as foreground group), refuses to run the agent without GO (in `terminal` mode GO arrives over the attempt socket with the attempt lock and cwd lease as `SCM_RIGHTS`, the peer uid is checked, and the gate runs in the pane, so the gate holds the attempt lock and outlives a dead supervisor), applies the environment scrub and the attempt writer id, reaps every orphan with `waitpid(-1)` for the whole attempt, enforces the hard ceiling (SIGTERM, `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs`, SIGKILL) on its own clock and publishes `gate-exit.json` once the domain is empty. `fgos internal gate`; same crate and spec as the supervisor. | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md#5-supervisor-and-gate) |
| Agent protocol (L3) | Pure per-CLI adapters (claude, codex, agy, pi, omp) that read what an agent CLI showed (capture tail, exit, outbox) and name the result (`completed`, `blocked(login\|trust-dialog\|usage-limit)`, `needs-human`, `exited`); decide stdin policy and the activity source for idle. Never builds argv (that stays with the executor configuration through `resolveExecutorCommand`), never retries, no dependency on terminal-control, locks or attempts. Direct and terminal adapters; the terminal ones read the pane through `AgentIo` (`screen`, `inspect`) wired by the supervisor to terminal-control. Crate `fgos-agent-protocol` (`packages/agent-protocol/rust`). | [agent-protocol/spec.md](agent-protocol/spec.md) |

| Dispatch Transport & Confinement | Machine backend registry, isolation confinement (`bwrap` v1 driver, attestation storage, fail-closed probes), executor adapters; the `bwrap` driver calls the credential renewal module at provisioning (`copyCredentialFiles`, the write-back marker) and removing a private home (`confinement/cleanup.mjs`) calls it again for write-back (dependency confinement → provider capacity, for the account lock only). | [../specs/confinement-authority.md](../specs/confinement-authority.md) |
| Run Result Evaluator | Evidence/confidence boundary for assignment run results. | [../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md](../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md) |
| Domain Components And Extension Layer | Domain-specific behavior, workflows, skills, task specs, doctrine. L2 prose no longer picks executors or mechanisms (lớp matching L2 cũ đã thu hồi per 0048); thin driver `fgos-run` delegates directly to the Workflow door (`fgos workflow start`) and P1 Execution Core (`fgos run`); a conductor names the Workflow case on each dispatch. | [../../domains/](../../domains/), [../architect/domainization/](../architect/domainization/) |
| Host And Surface Layer | CLI, fgos Gateway (REST/MCP/web), `herdr-dashboard` plugin and other Herdr surfaces into platform engines. | Host invocation and gateway docs |
| Packaging-Distribution | Runtime packaging, install, activation, setup/doctor readiness. | [packaging-distribution/README.md](packaging-distribution/README.md) |
| Knowledge, Learning, And Documentation Registry | Retrospective learning, doc registry, end-user docs index, trace/evolve signals. | Knowledge and docs registry docs |
| Observe (Metrics & Friction) | Measurement and friction tracking across substrate entities (cases, runs, sessions, friction, snapshots). Owned in Rust (`packages/observe/rust`), native routing. | [../specs/observe.md](../specs/observe.md) |
| Convention (Executable Names & Placement) | Platform-core authority for deterministic artifact names, repository-relative placement, path classification, and conformance checking. Implemented; owns no state and depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. | [convention/spec.md](convention/spec.md) |
| Session Identity (Writer Identity) | Foundation authority for "who is the writer of this process" (`{id, source}`). One implementation, the Rust crate `fgos-session-identity` (`packages/session-identity/rust`, native verb `fgos identity`); Observe calls it in process, Node through the facade `src/util/session-identity.mjs`. Also mints the writer id of an attempt (`att-<attemptId>`, route `fgos internal identity mint-attempt`) and carries the launcher's env scrub the gate applies. Owns no state and depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`; Observe depends on it; the run supervisor's controller half calls the mint. Grants no lock or claim authority. | [session-identity/spec.md](session-identity/spec.md) |
| Terminal-control (L2) | Foundation component for "which pane does this key run in" on a terminal multiplexer, usable without a run. Rust crate `fgos-terminal-control` (`packages/terminal-control/rust`) with a key-addressed upper port and a driver port with declared capabilities (herdr first; Windows declares none). Writes only the allocation record; closes only panes it allocated, never a tab; Node reaches it through the internal route `fgos internal terminal-control`, no user verb. Dependency one way: run supervisor → Terminal-control (the supervisor holds the key, the attempt id, never a pane). Node migration done; setup adds the `terminal` config section and `<stateRoot>/terminal`, doctor runs `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations`. | [terminal-control/spec.md](terminal-control/spec.md) |
| Process Facts & Control (L0) | Single authority for "is this process tuple `{host, bootId, pidNs, pid, startTime}` alive, dead or unknown" (`judge`, one shared vector file for Rust and Node), for signalling a process by identity (`pidfd` on Linux, never a bare pid), for spawning with an explicit fd mapping, and for the domain primitives `domain_is_empty`/`domain_kill_all` the predecessor rule of holder-lock needs. Never spawns to read facts, never kills by bare pid, never reads mtime, knows no run, lock or pane. Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), one driver per OS; the Node leaf `src/runner/dispatch/process-identity.mjs` reads the same vectors, and reconcile imports only `facts`. The gate primitives (subreaper, PDEATHSIG, PID namespace, tty) stay with the run supervisor; the containment port lives in this crate (row below). Depends only on the OS. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md) |
| Holder-lock (L1) | Single authority for "who holds which resource", as the kernel sees it: kernel locks on open file descriptions behind one OS-neutral port (`acquire`, `release`, `run_borrowed`, `probe`, `holders`, `guarantee`), the lock registry (`packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json`: every lock's kind, scope, rank, path, legacy shape and fence), lock order inside one `LockScope`, the description rules, the predecessor-domain rule, the single state-root resolution and the cutover fences. Never reads writer identity, never takes a lock from a live holder, never derives a decision from a pid, TTL or mtime. Rust crate `fgos-holder-lock` (`packages/holder-lock/rust`) plus the internal routes `fgos internal lock-fd|state-root|quiesce-scan|lock-borrow-vectors`; Node only through the facade `src/holder-lock/`, which never exposes an fd. Depends on Process Facts & Control and the kernel. Owns the cold locks (gateway, runner, sessions, advance, reconcile, recovery, full-suite, provider account/state, dispatch cwd) and the main checkout mutex (one door `withMainCheckout`, git children and the pre-commit hook borrow the lock through the description, no pid or TTL), the merge slot and `worktree-admin`; `fgos lock fence` is the one door for a hung live holder. `advance` follows Shape C (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), owner 2026-10-19, [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)): a conductor case holds it for one reserve or one release/settle; the Playbook proposer holds it for the life of its loop, so its holder is the proposer's liveness, as today; a dispatch naming a live playbook case from inside its own Unit is refused by name. `answer` never appends directly: it writes the gate-answer file and tries `advance` once. The worktree binding is one exclusively created file per worktree, not a registry row. No new lock row; rank stays 80; no re-rank for an Event Store cutover. It does not own the state store's hot mutex (`state`, `porting-events`: `withStateTx` in `src/state/hot-lock.mjs`, which replaced `events.lock`, `claims.lock` and `porting/events.lock`): the state store owns that mechanism, a temporary one until the store moves to Rust, and takes only its cleanup lock and the fences from this component. The main door's `.fgos` checkpoint is a detachable adapter, so the lock core knows nothing of the event log. | [holder-lock/spec.md](holder-lock/spec.md) |
| Containment port (L0) | Single authority for "which processes belong to this attempt, and are there any left": an OS-neutral process domain per attempt (`create`, `spawn_in`, `is_empty`, `kill_all`, `guarantee`) with one driver per OS (`bwrap-pidns` and `linux-pgroup` on Linux, `windows-job`, `macos-tree`), each reporting a guarantee level (`kernel` or `best-effort`) and its named escapes. Knows no attempt beyond the id that names a domain, and no envelope, lock or pane. Module `containment` of the Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), contract `packages/process/contracts/containment.port.v1.json`; depends only on the OS. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md#10-containment-port) |
| Git (foundation) | Single authority for repository facts, typed Git operations and their recovery WAL: every fgOS mutation of local objects, refs, index, worktrees and worktree registration, the local side of fetch and push, and operation recovery, through typed ports (Inspect, Refs, Worktree, ScopedCommit, Sync, Land, SafeRestore, RepositoryConfig, Remote, Recovery, Publication); no public `git(args)` port. Its Publication port is the only door to `refs/fgos/*`, and Event Store is the only production writer of event refs through it. Owns no business approval, Work lifecycle, event semantics or lock mechanism. Consumers: Workflow, Execution Core, Work, Event Store, setup. Depends on Holder-lock, Process Facts & Control and Session Identity; imports no consumer. Rust crate `fgos-git` (`packages/git/rust`, planned); Node reaches it only through the one combined N-API addon that also links `fgos-event-store`. Not implemented: today's Node git writers stay until the Git plan replaces them in one release per caller family. | [git/spec.md](git/spec.md) |
| Event Store | Signed design D-ADR0055; implementation not started. Owns event durability after `fsync`, sealing immutable git objects on per-machine `refs/fgos/events/<machine-id>`, publication/sync and deterministic union reads. One Rust core with a thin Node facade; consumer reducers and rebuildable views remain with consumers, claims/leases remain runtime state. Uses Process and Holder-lock; planned `event-seal` rank 58 and `event-append` rank 70 are specified, not yet registered or implemented. Work is the first consumer; porting, observe and decisions follow. Acceptance requires spec §23 gates; no current state-store ownership transfer is claimed. | [event-store/spec.md](event-store/spec.md) |
| Run Supervisor (L4) | One Rust process per attempt that owns the attempt after the controller handed it over: holds the attempt lock and the cwd lease, creates the containment domain, starts the launch gate, watches the soft deadline and idle, publishes the receipt and the per-step receipts, runs the post-receipt steps and owns the adopt door (`fgos internal adopt`, one door for resume, recover, scan and home cleanup). A supervisor that dies leaves the agent running; adopt settles it. Never knows a pane or a terminal, never picks a provider or retries, never judges the work (Run Result Evaluator inside the Node `settle-attempt` step). Crate `fgos-run-supervisor` (`packages/run-supervisor/rust`), routes `fgos internal supervise\|gate\|adopt\|attempt-step` (protocol 1, not in help), Node client and steps in `src/run-supervisor/`. Depends on Containment port, Process Facts & Control, Holder-lock and agent-protocol. Two launch modes: `direct` (headless process) and `terminal` (an agent in a terminal-control pane, addressed by the attempt id; the supervisor listens on an attempt socket, drives the pane through the agent protocol and ends with a `release-slot` step). Depends also on Terminal-control (in process, by key). | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md) |
| Launch gate (L4, part of the run supervisor) | The process root of the agent inside the containment domain (pid 1 of a fresh PID namespace on Linux): owns the agent's IO (capture files, stdin; in `terminal` mode the pane's tty, with the agent as foreground group), refuses to run the agent without GO (in `terminal` mode GO arrives over the attempt socket with the attempt lock and cwd lease as `SCM_RIGHTS`, the peer uid is checked, and the gate runs in the pane, so the gate holds the attempt lock and outlives a dead supervisor), applies the environment scrub and the attempt writer id, reaps every orphan with `waitpid(-1)` for the whole attempt, enforces the hard ceiling (SIGTERM, `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs`, SIGKILL) on its own clock and publishes `gate-exit.json` once the domain is empty. `fgos internal gate`; same crate and spec as the supervisor. | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md#5-supervisor-and-gate) |
| Agent protocol (L3) | Pure per-CLI adapters (claude, codex, agy, pi, omp) that read what an agent CLI showed (capture tail, exit, outbox) and name the result (`completed`, `blocked(login\|trust-dialog\|usage-limit)`, `needs-human`, `exited`); decide stdin policy and the activity source for idle. Never builds argv (that stays with the executor configuration through `resolveExecutorCommand`), never retries, no dependency on terminal-control, locks or attempts. Direct and terminal adapters; the terminal ones read the pane through `AgentIo` (`screen`, `inspect`) wired by the supervisor to terminal-control. Crate `fgos-agent-protocol` (`packages/agent-protocol/rust`). | [agent-protocol/spec.md](agent-protocol/spec.md) |

priorPassage.text:
| # | Element | Meaning | Values | Required | Default |
|---|-------|---------|--------|----------|---------|
| 1 | Package name | The npm package identity used for the git-based install command | `forgent` | yes | — |
| 2 | Package version | A semantic version string tooling (e.g. packaging commands) needs to treat the package as valid | semver string | yes | `0.1.0` |
| 3 | Distribution file allowlist | The exact set of paths shipped to anyone installing the package — everything else in the source repo is excluded | `bin`, `src`, `scripts`, `core`, `domains`, `.agents`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, the end-user documentation subset (`docs/how-to`, `docs/explanation`, and `docs/enduser-docs-index.json`), plus `packages/convention/contracts/convention.rules.v1.json`, which installed doctor needs to interpret per-rule cutoffs without duplicating native rule data | yes | — |
| 4 | CLI entry points | The commands exposed once installed | `fgos` → runs `bin/fgos.mjs`; `fgos-runner` → runs `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` (the autonomous-loop runner, see spec Runner) | yes | — |
| 4b | Claude Code plugin skill set | `plugins/fgOS/skills/` — the Claude Code plugin's own skill bundle, distributed via the Claude Code plugin marketplace mechanism (a separate distribution channel from the npm-installed `fgos`/`fgos-runner` CLI above). Ships two layers: hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills (`cook`, `discover`, `pick`, `submit`, ...) and mirrored `fgos-*` dev-skills plus `_shared/` for plugin-only consumers. Dev-skills are authored in `core/skills/` or `domains/*/skills/`; run `npm run build:skills` in the fgOS source repo to assemble `.agents/skills/`, generate `.claude/skills/` thin wrappers and references, and mirror dev-skills/shared fragments into the plugin. Plugin mirrors stay byte-identical to `.agents/skills/`, while Claude `SKILL.md` files are thin redirects with byte-identical frontmatter (`test/skills/fgos-mirror.test.mjs`). Assembled Markdown carries a generated-from source header. Do not hand-edit `.agents`, generated `.claude` files, or plugin mirrors; hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills remain sources. `plugin-dev-skills-packaged` (doctor check, row 7 below) detects missing or stale plugin mirrors | mirrored dev-skills + shared fragments + hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills | yes (the mirrors let plugin-only consumers dispatch dev-skills without a source checkout) | — |
| 5 | Dev checkout shell helper | An opt-in file, sourced from a contributor's own shell profile, exposing the same two CLI entry points from inside a checkout of the source repository — no install, no package fetch | one file, both commands | no (contributor's own choice) | not sourced automatically anywhere |
| 5b | Global config file | `~/.fgos/config.json` — same schema as the project-local shared config file, initialized/kept current by `fgos setup` (tsk-1ri) the same way it already handles the project-local file; project always wins any key present in both (`mergeWithGlobalConfig`, `src/config/global-config.mjs`) | one file, home-dir-relative | no (optional; a missing file is not an error, resolves to `{}`) | not created by anything except `fgos setup` |
| 5c | Machine backend registry file | `~/.fgos/confinement-backends.json` (overridable via `FGOS_CONFINEMENT_BACKEND_REGISTRY_PATH`) — machine-local backend registry declaring confinement backends (e.g. `bwrap`, container) available on the host (`confinement-backend-registry.v1`); managed by `fgos doctor --fix` (not project-over-global merge), trust store for security isolation drivers | one file, machine-local path | no (optional; bootstrap creates default bwrap backend on demand) | `~/.fgos/confinement-backends.json` |
| 5d | Provider-capacity runtime state | `~/.fgos/runtime/provider-capacity/state.json` — machine-local selected-account lease/quarantine state for provider-capacity rotation. Intentionally host-global only (never project-overridden) so multiple projects sharing provider accounts coordinate concurrency and rate limits safely without starvation. It is never packaged, never committed, and never repaired by `doctor`; `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` and the `provider-capacity-state` doctor check report it, while manual clear goes through `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity clear-quarantine ...`. An account locked for a dead login is also unlocked by one real call when a dispatch would otherwise find no usable account (the lazy-probe unlock rule, now in `docs/specs/runner.md`). Its locks are holder-lock kernel locks under the machine lock root (row 5g): `provider-state` guards this file, and `provider-account/<provider>/<account>` guards one account while a renewal or unlock probe runs through it, held until that call and every process it started have exited. The same directory holds `account-locks/<provider>/<account>/`: copies of a login renewed elsewhere and waiting to be applied, a scratch home while a renewal runs, and the renewal failure cooldown; it is created only when a renewal or write-back runs and holds no credential outside those copies. | one runtime directory, home-dir-relative | no (created only when a provider account lease/quarantine/write occurs) | absent/inactive |
| 5e | Confinement attestation store state | `~/.local/state/fgos/attestations/` (or `$XDG_STATE_HOME/fgos/attestations`, overridable via `FGOS_CONFINEMENT_ATTESTATION_STORE_PATH`) — host-global security attestation records. Intentionally host-global only (outside all agent write grants) so confined agents can never tamper with their own audit trails, preserving immutable attestation integrity across projects. | one directory, machine-local path | no (created on first confined dispatch attestation) | absent/inactive |
| 5f | Workspace customization folder | `fgos/` at the project root: tracked in the project's own git, written once as a skeleton at onboarding and never edited by fgOS afterwards. Holds the customer's own agent definitions (`fgos/agents/<name>.yaml`), which win over a definition of the same name in the installed set (RUL13 (customer customization lives in one tracked workspace folder)). Read by `--seats @name` (runner decision 0057); the `fgctl init` skeleton is not built yet | directory | no | absent — the installed set alone applies |
| 5g | Lock directories and the lock config key | `<lockRoot>` = `<stateRoot>/locks` (machine-scope lock files: `full-suite`, `provider-account/<provider>/<account>`, `provider-state`, `install`) and `<fgosDir>/locks` (repo-scope lock files: `gateway`, `runner`, `sessions`, `reconcile`, `main-checkout`, `worktree-admin`, `merge-slot--<encodeURIComponent(ref)>` per target ref, `state.hot` and `state.reclaim.lock`, `porting-events.hot` and `porting-events.reclaim.lock` (the state store's hot mutex: the `.hot` record is not a kernel lock file, only the `.reclaim.lock` file is), `activation`, `observe`, and `dispatch-cwd--<dev>-<ino>` keyed by the dispatch directory's identity after realpath; the run locks live in their run: `<workflowRunDir>/locks/advance.lock`, `<runDir>/locks/recovery.lock`), both created by `fgos setup` (the machine root with mode 0700); `stateRoot` is the single resolution of `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md` §11 (`FGOS_STATE_ROOT` pinned by the host, else `FGOS_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME/fgos`, `HOME/.local/state/fgos`). One config key, `lock.predecessorKillWaitMs` (`registerConfigDefault({id: 'lock', key: 'lock', shape: {predecessorKillWaitMs: 2000}})`): the longest wait, after the processes of a dead previous holder have been terminated, for them to exit before the lock is handed over; it never waits for a live domain to drain. Global first, project on top; the merge adds the key only when it is missing. Lock files are never packaged, committed or repaired; `lock-kernel-semantics`, `lock-holders`, `lock-record-unreadable`, `lock-fences`, `lock-predecessor-kill-wait` and `state-root` report them (row 7) | two directories plus one integer key | no (created by setup; the key defaults to 2000 ms when absent) | `lock: {predecessorKillWaitMs: 2000}` |
| 5h | Terminal-control directory and the `terminal` config key | `<stateRoot>/terminal` (one subdirectory per driver; allocation records and their markers, a cache of what the port opened: deleting it never closes a pane because nobody closes a pane that has no record), created by `fgos setup` with mode 0700 (the `terminal-dir` fix). One config key, `terminal` (`registerConfigDefault({id: 'terminal', key: 'terminal', shape: {allocationGraceMs: 60000, retainFailedPaneMs: null, layout: {policy: 'measured-split', minCols: 80, minRows: 20, maxPanesPerTab: 8}}})`); `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md` §9 gives each number's source. Project over global over default; the merge adds a missing key only. No new environment variable (`FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` stays, as the input of `attach`). Checked 2026-10-18: the release active in the forgentX, mdview and mcp-skill-hub workspaces (one digest) accepts a `terminal` section in the global and in the project config, so the key is written like `lock`; had it refused unknown keys, setup would have written it to the project config only until all three workspaces ran the new release. | `<stateRoot>/terminal` present / absent; config key present / absent | yes (computed, not stored) | — |

| 7 | Quyền sở-hữu gốc | Ai đang cầm mọi việc CON của một gốc trong MỘT lượt chạy — gắn lúc con đầu tiên của gốc được nhận, xả khi gốc xong; sống trong bộ nhớ của lượt chạy, KHÔNG bền qua lượt chạy khác/tiến trình khác | một định danh (per lượt chạy) | — | chưa-chủ |

| 9 | Candidate (Gate A, self-improve loop STR13 Slice 1) | Một việc mang ít nhất một bản ghi friction chưa ngã-ngũ, xếp hạng làm ứng viên tự cải thiện — dẫn xuất TỪ friction đã ghi, không phải một bản ghi độc lập, không bền qua lần `evolve` khác | id, disposition, errorClass, layer, detail, attempts (tất cả lấy từ bản ghi friction MỚI NHẤT theo dấu thời gian của id đó khi id có nhiều bản ghi chưa ngã-ngũ), score (cộng dồn TOÀN BỘ bản ghi chưa ngã-ngũ của id đó, không chỉ bản mới nhất) | — | dẫn xuất mỗi lần gọi `evolve` |

| # | Element | Meaning | Values | Required | Default |
|---|-------|---------|--------|----------|---------|
| 1 | Package name | The npm package identity used for the git-based install command | `forgent` | yes | — |
| 2 | Package version | A semantic version string tooling (e.g. packaging commands) needs to treat the package as valid | semver string | yes | `0.1.0` |
| 3 | Distribution file allowlist | The exact set of paths shipped to anyone installing the package — everything else in the source repo is excluded | `bin`, `src`, `scripts`, `core`, `domains`, `.agents`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, the end-user documentation subset (`docs/how-to`, `docs/explanation`, and `docs/enduser-docs-index.json`), plus `packages/convention/contracts/convention.rules.v1.json`, which installed doctor needs to interpret per-rule cutoffs without duplicating native rule data | yes | — |
| 4 | CLI entry points | The commands exposed once installed | `fgos` → runs `bin/fgos.mjs`; `fgos-runner` → runs `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` (the autonomous-loop runner, see spec Runner) | yes | — |
| 4b | Claude Code plugin skill set | `plugins/fgOS/skills/` — the Claude Code plugin's own skill bundle, distributed via the Claude Code plugin marketplace mechanism (a separate distribution channel from the npm-installed `fgos`/`fgos-runner` CLI above). Ships two layers: hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills (`cook`, `discover`, `pick`, `submit`, ...) and mirrored `fgos-*` dev-skills plus `_shared/` for plugin-only consumers. Dev-skills are authored in `core/skills/` or `domains/*/skills/`; run `npm run build:skills` in the fgOS source repo to assemble `.agents/skills/`, generate `.claude/skills/` thin wrappers and references, and mirror dev-skills/shared fragments into the plugin. Plugin mirrors stay byte-identical to `.agents/skills/`, while Claude `SKILL.md` files are thin redirects with byte-identical frontmatter (`test/skills/fgos-mirror.test.mjs`). Assembled Markdown carries a generated-from source header. Do not hand-edit `.agents`, generated `.claude` files, or plugin mirrors; hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills remain sources. `plugin-dev-skills-packaged` (doctor check, row 7 below) detects missing or stale plugin mirrors | mirrored dev-skills + shared fragments + hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills | yes (the mirrors let plugin-only consumers dispatch dev-skills without a source checkout) | — |
| 5 | Dev checkout shell helper | An opt-in file, sourced from a contributor's own shell profile, exposing the same two CLI entry points from inside a checkout of the source repository — no install, no package fetch | one file, both commands | no (contributor's own choice) | not sourced automatically anywhere |
| 5b | Global config file | `~/.fgos/config.json` — same schema as the project-local shared config file, initialized/kept current by `fgos setup` (tsk-1ri) the same way it already handles the project-local file; project always wins any key present in both (`mergeWithGlobalConfig`, `src/config/global-config.mjs`) | one file, home-dir-relative | no (optional; a missing file is not an error, resolves to `{}`) | not created by anything except `fgos setup` |
| 5c | Machine backend registry file | `~/.fgos/confinement-backends.json` (overridable via `FGOS_CONFINEMENT_BACKEND_REGISTRY_PATH`) — machine-local backend registry declaring confinement backends (e.g. `bwrap`, container) available on the host (`confinement-backend-registry.v1`); managed by `fgos doctor --fix` (not project-over-global merge), trust store for security isolation drivers | one file, machine-local path | no (optional; bootstrap creates default bwrap backend on demand) | `~/.fgos/confinement-backends.json` |
| 5d | Provider-capacity runtime state | `~/.fgos/runtime/provider-capacity/state.json` — machine-local selected-account lease/quarantine state for provider-capacity rotation. Intentionally host-global only (never project-overridden) so multiple projects sharing provider accounts coordinate concurrency and rate limits safely without starvation. It is never packaged, never committed, and never repaired by `doctor`; `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` and the `provider-capacity-state` doctor check report it, while manual clear goes through `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity clear-quarantine ...`. An account locked for a dead login is also unlocked by one real call when a dispatch would otherwise find no usable account (the lazy-probe unlock rule, now in `docs/specs/runner.md`). Its locks are holder-lock kernel locks under the machine lock root (row 5g): `provider-state` guards this file, and `provider-account/<provider>/<account>` guards one account while a renewal or unlock probe runs through it, held until that call and every process it started have exited. The same directory holds `account-locks/<provider>/<account>/`: copies of a login renewed elsewhere and waiting to be applied, a scratch home while a renewal runs, and the renewal failure cooldown; it is created only when a renewal or write-back runs and holds no credential outside those copies. | one runtime directory, home-dir-relative | no (created only when a provider account lease/quarantine/write occurs) | absent/inactive |
| 5e | Confinement attestation store state | `~/.local/state/fgos/attestations/` (or `$XDG_STATE_HOME/fgos/attestations`, overridable via `FGOS_CONFINEMENT_ATTESTATION_STORE_PATH`) — host-global security attestation records. Intentionally host-global only (outside all agent write grants) so confined agents can never tamper with their own audit trails, preserving immutable attestation integrity across projects. | one directory, machine-local path | no (created on first confined dispatch attestation) | absent/inactive |
| 5f | Workspace customization folder | `fgos/` at the project root: tracked in the project's own git, written once as a skeleton at onboarding and never edited by fgOS afterwards. Holds the customer's own agent definitions (`fgos/agents/<name>.yaml`), which win over a definition of the same name in the installed set (RUL13 (customer customization lives in one tracked workspace folder)). Read by `--seats @name` (runner decision 0057); the `fgctl init` skeleton is not built yet | directory | no | absent — the installed set alone applies |
| 5g | Lock directories and the lock config key | `<lockRoot>` = `<stateRoot>/locks` (machine-scope lock files: `full-suite`, `provider-account/<provider>/<account>`, `provider-state`, `install`) and `<fgosDir>/locks` (repo-scope lock files: `gateway`, `runner`, `sessions`, `reconcile`, `main-checkout`, `worktree-admin`, `merge-slot--<encodeURIComponent(ref)>` per target ref, `state.hot` and `state.reclaim.lock`, `porting-events.hot` and `porting-events.reclaim.lock` (the state store's hot mutex: the `.hot` record is not a kernel lock file, only the `.reclaim.lock` file is), `activation`, `observe`, and `dispatch-cwd--<dev>-<ino>` keyed by the dispatch directory's identity after realpath; the run locks live in their run: `<workflowRunDir>/locks/advance.lock`, `<runDir>/locks/recovery.lock`), both created by `fgos setup` (the machine root with mode 0700); `stateRoot` is the single resolution of `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md` §11 (`FGOS_STATE_ROOT` pinned by the host, else `FGOS_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME/fgos`, `HOME/.local/state/fgos`). One config key, `lock.predecessorKillWaitMs` (`registerConfigDefault({id: 'lock', key: 'lock', shape: {predecessorKillWaitMs: 2000}})`): the longest wait, after the processes of a dead previous holder have been terminated, for them to exit before the lock is handed over; it never waits for a live domain to drain. Global first, project on top; the merge adds the key only when it is missing. Lock files are never packaged, committed or repaired; `lock-kernel-semantics`, `lock-holders`, `lock-record-unreadable`, `lock-fences`, `lock-predecessor-kill-wait` and `state-root` report them (row 7) | two directories plus one integer key | no (created by setup; the key defaults to 2000 ms when absent) | `lock: {predecessorKillWaitMs: 2000}` |
| 5h | Terminal-control directory and the `terminal` config key | `<stateRoot>/terminal` (one subdirectory per driver; allocation records and their markers, a cache of what the port opened: deleting it never closes a pane because nobody closes a pane that has no record), created by `fgos setup` with mode 0700 (the `terminal-dir` fix). One config key, `terminal` (`registerConfigDefault({id: 'terminal', key: 'terminal', shape: {allocationGraceMs: 60000, retainFailedPaneMs: null, layout: {policy: 'measured-split', minCols: 80, minRows: 20, maxPanesPerTab: 8}}})`); `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md` §9 gives each number's source. Project over global over default; the merge adds a missing key only. No new environment variable (`FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` stays, as the input of `attach`). Checked 2026-10-18: the release active in the forgentX, mdview and mcp-skill-hub workspaces (one digest) accepts a `terminal` section in the global and in the project config, so the key is written like `lock`; had it refused unknown keys, setup would have written it to the project config only until all three workspaces ran the new release. | `<stateRoot>/terminal` present / absent; config key present / absent | yes (computed, not stored) | — |
| 6 | Config staleness | Whether a config file (project-local or global — same computation, tsk-1ri) already has every setting the current default schema defines | up to date / missing one or more default settings | yes (computed, not stored) | — |
| 7 | Doctor check | One named diagnostic `fgos doctor` reports on | not a fixed list — an extensible registry (`src/setup/registrations.mjs`'s `registerCheck`); a check registration and a config-default registration are independent, never a forced pairing — a module may register only a check, only a config-default, or both. Today's registered checks: `convention-conformance`, `node-version-and-git`, `cli-version-visible` (tsk-2ej), `shell-integration-sourced`, `project-fgos-launcher` (a release install has one fgos launcher on PATH that runs each project's own activated fgos, see RUL17 (one fgos on PATH runs each project's own activated fgos)), `config-not-stale`, `main-checkout-hook-wired`, `tool-registry-configured`, `work-classification-vocabulary`, `work-step-vocabulary` (tsk-64h), `domain-workflow-operations-coverage`, `root-drift`, `delivered-not-on-trunk` (tsk-1l9), `config-awareness`, `provider-capacity-state` (reports account lease/quarantine state and never auto-clears), `credential-copies-retained` (login copies still pending for a renewal after a day, and private homes held after repeated staging failures, counted by provider/account and age; read-only, a held home fails, copies waiting for a renewal only warn, and, when the machine-global provider inventory was read, copies of any age in a store directory the account's login store layout no longer reads fail, naming the directory for hand recovery (when the global config cannot be read or is refused by the validator the check fails, says the layout was not checked with the reason, lists copies at any age and promises nothing about a dispatch); interrupted stagings (pending/.tmp-*) are reported too once their writer is gone and they have sat for ten minutes, and the over-limit line names the store; kept homes under a registered backend's temp and private-home roots are scanned, which the orphan reaper check does not do, and one there counts as held at once because nothing retries it; the check itself never deletes and never prints a value), `lock-kernel-semantics` (for the workspace lock directory and the machine lock root: the holder-lock driver's guarantee through the host's lock-fd route, then a two-process probe on that same mount, a description locked here and handed to a child must read held while the child lives and free once it died; prints driver, exclusion, borrow and holders levels; kernel with a green probe passes, a missing directory warns until setup creates it, a guarantee of unsupported (a platform with no driver) and a network filesystem none fail by name; on Windows the probe runs over a lock-hold helper and the message shows lockfileex), `lock-borrow-vectors` (runs the host's lock-borrow-vectors route: a lock description borrowed by a git child must not leak to any background process git starts; any red vector or a red sibling check fails, unavailable fails, since activation refuses the same result and there is no run-time switch that disables borrowing; runs on Windows with its own pid-handle assertion), `lock-holders` (for every existing lock file of the locks this release cut over, including the main checkout, merge slot and worktree-admin files, the holders the kernel lists: a holder that is neither a fgOS process, by the host's state-root pin or a fgOS payload in its argv, nor a borrowed child of that lock warns with pid and cmdline; a predecessor record next to a lock file naming a domain that is not empty, an unknown record version or a Windows job the host does not judge empty (read-only, through the host's lock-fd route with --predecessor-state) warns with the domain and the reason; holders that cannot be listed are informational), `lock-record-unreadable` (the state and porting-events hot records of the workspace, under .fgos/locks: a record that does not parse, or one whose holder the judge cannot place for more than five minutes, warns with the path and the fence command of the lock verb; absent, alive or dead holders pass; no automatic fix, because a person confirms the holder is gone; never fails), `lock-fences` (every legacy lock path of the registry has its cutover fence, tombstone or blocking generation (the main checkout lock, one merge slot per local branch and the three old state store locks, the old events, claims and porting events lock files, among them); a missing one warns and names the fix, and an old lock file still present is named because it blocks that fix), `lock-predecessor-kill-wait` (reads lock.predecessorKillWaitMs from the project config, else the global one, prints the value and its source; not an integer from 1 to 60000 fails by name, an unparseable config fails; absent passes with the default 2000), `state-root` (state root, lock root and their source as Node resolves them and as the Rust host answers for the same environment; a difference fails; a pinned root also shows what the host resolves without the pin), `dependencies-installed`, `gate-bypass-configured`, `claude-plugin-marketplace`, `plugin-skill-cli-reachable`, `plugin-dev-skills-packaged` (tsk-32b), `changelog-unreleased-stale`, `herdr-launcher-configured`, `herdr-web-dashboard-configured` (tsk-48w), `enduser-docs-index-stale` (tsk-1m0), `invariant-checks-configured` (tsk-516), `invocation-git-write-grants` (warns when an invocation or executor still grants a git add or git commit tool; the runner commits, workers only edit files; read-only, never rewrites user config), `worktree-setup-configured` (a present worktreeSetup section is a list of non-empty shell commands every runner-created worktree runs after its dependency install; never executes them), `events-jsonl-not-truncated` (tsk-cgg), `worker-slots-ceiling-usable` (tsk-1oz), `gateway-token-configured` (tsk-4r1), `readme-install-tag-exists` (tsk-2t8), `iron-law-configured` (tsk-1y6-1), `leaf-notify-drift` (tsk-1el), `task-specs-resolve` (tsk-2t9c), `agent-claims-resolve` (tsk-2t9c), `agent-type-names-unique` (tsk-397-12; | # | Element | Meaning | Values | Required | Default |
|---|-------|---------|--------|----------|---------|
| 1 | Package name | The npm package identity used for the git-based install command | `forgent` | yes | — |
| 2 | Package version | A semantic version string tooling (e.g. packaging commands) needs to treat the package as valid | semver string | yes | `0.1.0` |
| 3 | Distribution file allowlist | The exact set of paths shipped to anyone installing the package — everything else in the source repo is excluded | `bin`, `src`, `scripts`, `core`, `domains`, `.agents`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, the end-user documentation subset (`docs/how-to`, `docs/explanation`, and `docs/enduser-docs-index.json`), plus `packages/convention/contracts/convention.rules.v1.json`, which installed doctor needs to interpret per-rule cutoffs without duplicating native rule data | yes | — |
| 4 | CLI entry points | The commands exposed once installed | `fgos` → runs `bin/fgos.mjs`; `fgos-runner` → runs `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` (the autonomous-loop runner, see spec Runner) | yes | — |
| 4b | Claude Code plugin skill set | `plugins/fgOS/skills/` — the Claude Code plugin's own skill bundle, distributed via the Claude Code plugin marketplace mechanism (a separate distribution channel from the npm-installed `fgos`/`fgos-runner` CLI above). Ships two layers: hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills (`cook`, `discover`, `pick`, `submit`, ...) and mirrored `fgos-*` dev-skills plus `_shared/` for plugin-only consumers. Dev-skills are authored in `core/skills/` or `domains/*/skills/`; run `npm run build:skills` in the fgOS source repo to assemble `.agents/skills/`, generate `.claude/skills/` thin wrappers and references, and mirror dev-skills/shared fragments into the plugin. Plugin mirrors stay byte-identical to `.agents/skills/`, while Claude `SKILL.md` files are thin redirects with byte-identical frontmatter (`test/skills/fgos-mirror.test.mjs`). Assembled Markdown carries a generated-from source header. Do not hand-edit `.agents`, generated `.claude` files, or plugin mirrors; hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills remain sources. `plugin-dev-skills-packaged` (doctor check, row 7 below) detects missing or stale plugin mirrors | mirrored dev-skills + shared fragments + hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills | yes (the mirrors let plugin-only consumers dispatch dev-skills without a source checkout) | — |
| 5 | Dev checkout shell helper | An opt-in file, sourced from a contributor's own shell profile, exposing the same two CLI entry points from inside a checkout of the source repository — no install, no package fetch | one file, both commands | no (contributor's own choice) | not sourced automatically anywhere |
| 5b | Global config file | `~/.fgos/config.json` — same schema as the project-local shared config file, initialized/kept current by `fgos setup` (tsk-1ri) the same way it already handles the project-local file; project always wins any key present in both (`mergeWithGlobalConfig`, `src/config/global-config.mjs`) | one file, home-dir-relative | no (optional; a missing file is not an error, resolves to `{}`) | not created by anything except `fgos setup` |
| 5c | Machine backend registry file | `~/.fgos/confinement-backends.json` (overridable via `FGOS_CONFINEMENT_BACKEND_REGISTRY_PATH`) — machine-local backend registry declaring confinement backends (e.g. `bwrap`, container) available on the host (`confinement-backend-registry.v1`); managed by `fgos doctor --fix` (not project-over-global merge), trust store for security isolation drivers | one file, machine-local path | no (optional; bootstrap creates default bwrap backend on demand) | `~/.fgos/confinement-backends.json` |
| 5d | Provider-capacity runtime state | `~/.fgos/runtime/provider-capacity/state.json` — machine-local selected-account lease/quarantine state for provider-capacity rotation. Intentionally host-global only (never project-overridden) so multiple projects sharing provider accounts coordinate concurrency and rate limits safely without starvation. priorPassage.title: Unheaded block 102
priorPassage.sample: - `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` — CLI (--once/--dry-run/--watch/--poll-ms — str7-str8-priority-intent; `--config` bỏ ở RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit
priorPassage.text:
- `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` — CLI (--once/--dry-run/--watch/--poll-ms — str7-str8-priority-intent; `--config` bỏ ở RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each)), exit theo phạm trù; nhánh `--watch` đăng ký `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` lên một `AbortController` chung TRƯỚC khi gọi `runWatch`, tín hiệu thứ hai buộc `process.exit(130)`; hàm `printResult` (dùng chung giữa `--once` và `onCycle` của `--watch`) nay bọc `result` (trừ `exitCode`) qua `wrapEnvelope` (`src/state/envelope.mjs`, cùng hàm `bin/fgos.mjs` dùng) và in JSON một dòng — không `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` như `fgos.mjs` — vì `--watch` phát nhiều phong bì nối tiếp theo thời gian (per str46-io-contract, xem RUL61 (kết-cục cuối của `fgos-runner` nay bọc cùng phong bì máy-đọc `fgos.v1` như mọi verb)); exit-code prose ở đầu file trỏ về `src/state/store.mjs`'s `EXIT_CODES` + `src/runner/loop.mjs`'s `EXIT_BUSY` thay vì tự liệt lại bảng
- `src/runner/loop.mjs` — vòng + startup reap (SKIP claim `human`/`session` — xem "Gặt-lại lúc khởi động") + khoá liên-tiến-trình `.fgos/locks/runner.lock` (kernel lease qua holder-lock; busy exit 6, nêu pid holder do kernel liệt kê); NGAY SAU reap, TRƯỚC vòng dispatch: (1) quét mọi item `stage==='discovery' && status==='todo'` (không đọc `item.mode`), dựng worktree tạm + `spawnWorker` với `stage: 'discovery'` cho từng item, đọc khối phán quyết trong output của worker rồi gọi `resolveDiscovery` (`src/intake/discovery.mjs`) với chính verdict đó, truyền `'runner'` — nhánh không có commit nào, hoặc không đọc được verdict, thì item được để nguyên tại chỗ cho lượt sau; (2) đọc lại view tươi rồi quét mọi item ở `stageForStep(domain,'Divide')` (`planning`) CỘNG tên di sản `decompose`, với `status==='todo'`, và gọi `resolvePlan` (`src/intake/plan.mjs`) cho từng item, cùng truyền `'runner'` — không kèm verdict, nên nó chỉ cho đi thẳng khi `plan.md` của item khai mode `tiny`/`small`, còn lại no-op an toàn; cùng lượt chạy có thể chaining cả hai sweep trên một item vừa rời `discovery`; ghi bản outcome dự đoán tại claim + thực tế ở cả hai lối ra cuối (thành đề xuất, hoặc đỗ/dừng) qua `addOutcome` của store; mọi `moveWork` runner tự gọi (claim/propose/park) truyền `role:'runner'`; gọi `runGoalCheck` (từ `goal-check.mjs`, không còn tự triển khai) cho cả proof lúc dispatch lẫn proof lúc gặt-lại; ngay trước khi spawn worker, đọc lại view TƯƠI qua `listWork(dir)` rồi truyền `feedback: {answer: view.gates?.[item.id]?.answer, reason: view.work?.[item.id]?.reason}` vào `spawnWorker` (per worker-execution STR33 / 396d9d9e, xem RUL23 (phản hồi người threading vào prompt worker)); `dispatch.mjs` — prompt/config/spawn (argv-only, spawnSync timeout; caveat grandchild SIGTERM ghi trong doc comment) + `resolveExecutorCommand`/`resolveTierModel` (dùng chung cho mọi lượt spawn worker, kể cả lượt dispatch nghiên-cứu — không còn call site nào cho một lời gọi model phán lồng bên trong engine); `buildPrompt(work, feedback?)` dựng 5 section cố định (Goal, Description, Worktree boundary, Expected proof, Constraints — hợp đồng test pin presence) cộng mục `# Human feedback` TÙY CHỌN khi `feedback.answer`/`feedback.reason` có mặt (nguyên văn, xem RUL23 (phản hồi người threading vào prompt worker)); `description` là `work.description` nguyên văn, degrade "(không có)" khi vắng (per discovery-context STR30); `spawnWorker(work, cfg, cwd, opts)` nhận `opts.feedback` truyền xuống `buildPrompt`; `worktree.mjs` — lifecycle + reclaimOrphanedCheckout + `detectTrunk(repoRoot)`/`isMainWorktree(repoRoot)` (dời từ `merge.mjs` sang đây per tsk-49i — cả hai là danh tính worktree/nhánh, không mang ngữ nghĩa nội dung merge; dời đi cũng cắt luôn import vòng `merge.mjs` ↔ `worktree.mjs`) + `createBranchRef(repoRoot, id, opts)` (tạo `fgw/<id>` chỉ-là-ref, không worktree, idempotent) + `createWorktree`'s `opts.baseRef` (fork worktree mới từ một ref chỉ định thay vì HEAD hiện tại — dùng cho con fork từ tip nhánh gốc); `recovery.mjs` — 8 lớp; `anti-loop.mjs` — `visitCount` (lifetime, dùng cho outcome/metric) + `visitsSinceLastHumanEvent(events, id)` (ngân sách CỔNG, per-item, reset trên `role==='human'` mang `answer` hoặc `reason`, xem RUL29 (cổng chống-lặp reset theo can thiệp người cuối cùng của chính việc)) + breaker; `loop.mjs`'s gate (cả nhánh dry-run đơn lẻ lẫn nhánh lọc `overLimit` của batch dispatch dưới) gọi `visitsSinceLastHumanEvent`, không còn `visitCount`, để quyết park; `createMissBreaker` nay PER-ITEM (Map theo id, `consecutiveMissesFor(itemId)`; lần hai dính bẩn thì không `update-ref`/không đồng bộ cây, trả `blocked` với lý do này, cùng hình dạng "chưa chạm gì, thử lại được" như `lock-lost-mid-merge`) (tsk-18a một lần `git merge --no-commit --no-ff` gãy mà KHÔNG tạo `MERGE_HEAD` — không phải xung đột văn bản thật — nên catchup coi là ứng viên thử lại tốt nhất, vì lần gãy này rất có thể chỉ do điều kiện nhất thời; tsk-4hj `merge-blocked-other-item` — `MERGE_HEAD` đã có sẵn TRƯỚC lần merge này, thuộc về một việc KHÁC đang nhập dở, cũng là ứng viên thử lại tốt vì việc kia rồi sẽ xong hoặc bị hủy) và nhánh riêng của việc còn tồn tại (`branchExists`); đích = `branchNameFor(resolveRoot(view,id))` nếu là con, `'main'` nếu là gốc/độc lập; mở worktree ephemeral trên chính nhánh của việc, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <đích> HEAD` TRƯỚC khi nhập → nhánh đã chứa đích rồi (exit 0) → bỏ hẳn merge lẫn commit (merge sẽ là no-op, `git commit` sau đó chết vì "nothing to commit" và việc kẹt `blocked` vĩnh viễn), vẫn chạy `runGoalCheck` thật trên cây hiện có → đỏ → giữ nguyên `blocked`, KHÔNG gọi `git merge --abort` (không có merge nào đang chạy) → xanh → `moveWork(..., to:'awaiting-approval')` với `outcome: 'already-caught-up'`, không tạo commit nào; chưa chứa đích (exit 1) → `git merge --no-commit --no-ff <đích>` → xung đột thật → `git merge --abort` + giữ nguyên `blocked`; sạch → `runGoalCheck` trên cây đã stage TRƯỚC khi commit → đỏ → `git merge --abort` + giữ nguyên `blocked`; xanh → commit rồi `moveWork(..., to:'awaiting-approval', expectedStatus:'blocked')` — cạnh, không `reason`, không qua `doing` (spike `.bee/spikes/fan-out-parallel/catchup-real-conflict-probe.sh` chứng minh trước khi build cell); một sự-kiện merge THỰC HIỆN TRỰC TIẾP trong verb này (không gọi `mergeRunnerItem` — hướng nhập của catch-up ngược với `mergeRunnerItem`, đích nhập VÀO nhánh của việc chứ không phải nhánh của việc nhập vào đích)
