There is no default-pool key. A run uses the first entry served by the family's own pool (`resolveTierModel`); `resolveTierCandidates` returns every entry for `fgos dispatch explain` and doctor. An entry served by another pool is accepted and never run until the lease routes pools; a cell with no entry for the family's pool counts as a missing tier, which still falls back to the executor's own `model` or the CLI default. *(Superseded by RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool): every entry is a candidate of the walk, run when its pool can serve the invocation, and a family with no cell at the tier refuses `tier-cell-missing`; the `executor.model` and CLI-default fallthrough is deleted.)* The project config accepts every form. The global `~/.fgos/config.json` is read by every fgOS release on the machine, and an older release fails on a list and passes `model@pool` to the CLI as a model id, so a list or `@` cell there is dropped with a warning naming the cell (once per process), and doctor `global-model-policies-portable` fails on it. Each agent family (`providerModel`) is served by exactly one executor; its transports (headless cli, herdr pane, sandboxed or not) are invocations of that executor, and `bind()` picks the pane invocation inside herdr and a cli one outside, so a capability gets the same family and model in both places. Doctor `executor-family-unique` fails on a family with two agent executors. `runner.llmAccounts..` is the machine's account inventory, global-only: `credentialStore: { : }` (`~`, `${HOME}` and `$HOME` expand), plus optional `label` and `disabled`. A pool name is the family name for the family's own vendor and the provider's name otherwise (`openrouter`); it may not contain `@` nor be another spelling of a configured family (`codex`, `openai-codex`, `glm`, `agy`). `readLlmAccounts` reports problems instead of throwing; `compareWithLegacyInventory` sets it against `runner.providers..accounts` by the state key the lease uses (`openai` is `openai-codex` there). The lease, account pins and credential provisioning read a pool from `runner.llmAccounts` when it declares the pool, and from `runner.providers` for a pool it does not declare (the transition read, RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool)). Doctor: `llm-accounts-shape` fails on any reader problem, `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` warns on accounts or login directories that differ once `llmAccounts` is declared (the comparison stays needed while both inventories are read), `model-policy-pools` warns on a cell naming a pool `llmAccounts` does not declare (the walk skips such an entry), `tier-fallback` warns on a family `runner.tierFallback` lists that has no cell at that tier or no agent executor. `fgos dispatch explain --for [--rigor ]` binds the capability through `bind()` and reports the family and the `prefer` entry that chose it, the tier, its source (rigor, override) and its ceiling (RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling)), the candidates in walk order (each with the reason it is out: `tier-cell-missing`, `pool-unusable`), the walk a seat takes when each binding fails, the entries of the primary's cell (`used`, `fallback`, `unusable` with the reason), and the accounts of every pool on the walk in the order the lease takes them with whether the CLI can run on each. It leases, spawns and writes nothing. - **RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling, 2026-10-17).** `runner.maxTier`, when set, is the highest tier a seat runs at, whatever asked for the tier: the unit's rigor, the capability's rigor floor, or an override (`--override '{"tier":...}'`). A capability that declares its own `rigor` in `runner.capabilities` raises the ceiling for its own seats to `rigorToTier[rigor]` when that tier is higher. The ceiling of a seat is therefore the higher of `runner.maxTier` and the tier of its capability's declared rigor (`resolveTierCeiling` in `bind.mjs`); a unit's rigor and an override stay under it, so only the config decides which capabilities may run above the cap, and a frontier override on a capability declaring `high` stops at `flagship`. Without `runner.maxTier` there is no ceiling. A capability cannot be held below the global cap this way. The binding records the ceiling on `provenance.tier.ceiling` as `{ value, source }`, `source` being `global` or `capability-rigor(, )`; a clamped tier's source reads `clamped:maxTier(, )`. `fgos dispatch explain` shows the ceiling, and doctor `capability-rigor-ceiling` lists the capabilities lifted above `runner.maxTier` with the tier and model they run at; it never fails. The assignment policy (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`) raises the tier `bind()` hands it and applies no ceiling, so when `bind()` clamped, the policy's recorded tier can read higher than the tier that ran; the model is always the one `bind()` chose. - **RUL104 (`fgos run --resume` after a controller death takes the settled attempt through adopt and never runs the agent twice; Ctrl-C cancels; 2026-10-18; owner decision 2026-10-16).** A unit whose controller died never continues on its own: it reads `unitState: awaiting-resume` (last attempt `closed`, no `unit-summary.json`, no live controller; shown by `dispatch inspect`, `dispatch show-run` and `fgos run --json`) and only an explicit `--resume` goes on. Resume asks adopt about the last attempt of every seat and round before anything else: `closed` with a result is the attempt's result and the unit carries on from it (commit `writes`, reviewer, next attempt, `unit-summary.json`), so the agent runs once; a `cancelled`, `abandoned-not-started` or `abandoned-before-brief` receipt is superseded, a new attempt runs the unit again and names the old one in `supersedesRunId` (set only on a new launch; the old attempt reads `superseded`); a `gate-lost` receipt (binding present, gate dead, no `gate-exit`) is not relaunched, a named limit: adopt cannot prove the agent never ran, so it fails closed (r6 §9.7) rather than risk running it twice, and the person starts a new `fgos run`; `running` and `being-adopted` are refused `attempt-still-running` (resume does not wait); `legacy-run` is refused `attempt-legacy-run` (doctor `legacy-attempts-stuck` settles it as `abandoned-legacy`, which is closed for the unit); a second concurrent `--resume` of the unit finds the controller seat (`unit-control` ledger) held by a live controller and is refused `resume-in-progress`. Resume never starts a second supervisor for an attempt that already has a binding or a receipt. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM publishes `cancel-requested.json` for every attempt the controller handed over, waits for their receipts for at most `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` (default `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` + 5000, minimum 1000) and exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) after printing the resume command; a second signal exits at once. `fgos dispatch recover` over a supervised attempt recommends `adopt`; `outbox/result-N.json` is evidence for it, never a reason to park. Mechanism and tables: [run-supervisor spec, section 9.1](../platform/run-supervisor/spec.md#91-controller-death). - **RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads; the driver hands over exactly that store's files, 2026-10-19).** A confined `cli` invocation may declare `credentialStore: { use, homeEnv, files? }` in the config: `use` is the store key (`codex`, `pi`, `omp`, a lowercase key; it replaces the basename of `command` as the key into an account's `credentialSources`), `homeEnv` is the environment variable its CLI reads its login home from, and `files` (optional, non-empty, relative, no `..`, no repeats) lists what to hand over. The config door refuses a malformed store and a store on an invocation with no confinement backend (an unconfined invocation reads its store in place through `env`; that path is not redesigned). One function, `credentialStoreOf` (`provider-capacity.mjs`), reads it for every consumer; an invocation that declares none but binds `private-home` to an env variable (the machine-global config and other projects still carry that older form) gets `{ use: , homeEnv: }`, and that inference is the only remaining reader of `resourceBindings`; it goes when those configs have moved. The confinement request carries `invocation.credentialStore` in place of the generic `resourceBindings` (the contract keeps its name `confinement-request.v1`; nothing outside the repo reads the field). The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. Trust seeding, write-back and refresh-ahead keep reading the leased account's store, now chosen by the store key. `dispatch explain` names the store of the bound invocation and whether it is declared or inferred; `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` (same id) covers every confined invocation that reads a store, notes absent files and fails only when none is present. In this repo's committed config the invocations of one CLI under one executor collapse into one (`pi-cli-bwrap`; the account is leased at launch), invocation ids no longer carry an account name (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`), and the OpenRouter key variable left the pi `env` because pi reads the key from the store's `auth.json` (measured 2026-10-19: with the key variables unset and only the three store files, pi answered). Not changed: leasing, quarantine, `llmAccounts`, the account inventory shape; the leased account is still chosen before the invocation is known, so an account that has no file of the store fails late (B1 filters accounts by store key before the lease), and the older fields stay in the committed config until the release that reads `credentialStore` is active. - **RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order and its cell entries; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine are per pool; a missing cell refuses by name, 2026-10-20).** Owner decisions 2026-10-19 (plan `261019-2312-model-pool-b1-fallback-and-account-order`), the walk of RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)'s cells made real. **Candidates.** `bind()` expands each `prefer` executor into one candidate per entry of its family's cell at the seat's tier (RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)), in cell order: `{ executor, invocation, pool, model }`; an entry without `@` is the family-named pool. `provenance.model.source` reads `modelPolicies..[]` (it read `resolveTierModel(.)`). A seat that leases an account (an out-of-process agent that is not a tool) needs the cell; an in-process, inline or tool seat needs none and binds with `pool: null`. **Primary.** The first binding follows `prefer` order exactly as before, with the soft family spread of the panel seats unchanged, so council seats keep leading with different families. **After a failure** the walk takes, in order: the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.` lists, limited to the families `prefer` names (a list narrows and never widens); with no list for the tier, the rest of the `prefer` order after the failed candidate. A walk never leaves its tier. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ : [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** - **`verify` stays on the Unit.** `validateUnit` keeps `verify` (a non-empty shell command) and `skills` (a non-empty list of skill names, trimmed, de-duplicated) through validation, the units-file loader, the workflow template and the round; a registered workflow template may set both too. - **Where the verify command comes from.** `verifyCommandOf` (`patterns/reviewed.mjs`) reads the Unit's own `verify`, else its capability's `verify`, and nothing else; the `code-change` preset pins none (it used to name `npm test`, which no runner ever executed, so a reviewed run recorded a verify pass that checked nothing), and `params.verify` no longer counts. A reviewed run with no verify command still passes on its checkers but its result carries `verify: { ran: false, reason }`; a solo or panel run, which has no verify step, says nothing. - **One bounded runner.** The verify step runs through `runCommand` (`src/runner/goal-check.mjs`, the same runner `return` and `approve` use) in the Unit's worktree, for at most `runner.timeoutMs` (the existing key and default; no new key, so nothing new for setup or doctor to register). A non-zero exit, a command that could not start and one that ran past the limit are each a failed verify that becomes findings naming the status (`exited N`, `timed out after Nms`, `could not run`) and the last twenty lines of output; none of them hangs the run. - **One-liner flags.** `fgos run "" --input , --verify ""` set the Unit's `inputs` and `verify`; both are refused beside `--unit` or `--resume`, and an empty value is refused before any unit run exists. - **Skills reach `bind()`.** `bind()` skips an executor whose `supports.skills` (new optional key in the executor's `supports` block, a non-empty array of names) does not list every skill the Unit names; none left refuses with reason `skills-unavailable` naming the missing skills, and the session lead never takes over such a Unit inline. Only roles that do the Unit's work are asked for skills: checker and panel roles (`reviewer`, `red-team`, `tester`, `panelist*`, `synthesizer`) are chosen on independence alone. An executor that declares no `supports.skills` provides none. - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work. - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11).

priorPassage.text:

Một cửa: `withMainCheckout(scope, purpose, fn)` acquire `main-checkout` (hạng 50, `<fgosDir>/locks/main-checkout.lock`) trong `LockScope` của caller và trao `mainHandle`; checkpoint `.fgos` (`runOpportunisticMainCheckoutChecks`) chạy trọn add → commit → reset-khi-lỗi dưới handle đó và BẮT BUỘC nhận handle từ caller, không bao giờ tự acquire: caller đã giữ main (claim, merge không slot) truyền handle của mình xuống, caller chỉ giữ merge slot gọi `withMainCheckout` trước; không có handle thì checkpoint không commit. Merge slot là mutex theo nhánh đích (hạng 20, `merge-slot--<encodeURIComponent(ref)>.lock`), `worktree-admin` (hạng 40) chỉ bọc `git worktree add` của runner (`remove`, `prune` không bọc). Thứ tự lock trong một scope kiểm theo hạng và ném `lock-order-violation` ngay. Mỗi git con của checkpoint/merge chạy qua `runBorrowed` (giao đúng description đã khóa cho con, `FGOS_LOCK_FD=main-checkout:3`, luôn thêm `-c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false`), thay `FGOS_MAIN_LOCK_HOLDER_PID`; hợp đồng `packages/holder-lock/contracts/main-checkout-borrow.v1.json`. Holder sống mà treo: `fgos lock fence <tên>` (không bao giờ giành lock từ holder sống), thay `fgos unlock`. Dispatch cwd lock dùng chung facade nhưng thuộc registry hàng `dispatch-cwd`, không phải hàng `main-checkout`. Manifest layer: infra.
- `src/util/session-identity.mjs` (STR65; ở `src/runner/` cho tới tsk-49i — dời sang `util/` để `state/store.mjs` không phải import ngược sang `runner/`) — `resolveWriterIdentity(fgosDir, {env, pid, execFile})` → `{id, source}`: ưu tiên `FGOS_SESSION_ID`/`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` làm `id` chuỗi; registry `<fgosDir>/sessions.json` chỉ ĐỐI CHIẾU giá trị đó, không bao giờ tự cấp một danh tính — khớp một `row.sessionId` → `source: 'registry'`, không khớp → `source: 'env'` (không có luật khớp theo thư mục hay pid của row, per str46-io-contract). Vắng cả hai biến môi trường (hoặc giá trị sai charset) thì đi ngược tối đa 3 tầng tiến trình cha (shell ra `ps -o ppid=`, dừng sớm ở pid 1 hoặc lỗi `ps`) lấy một pid số làm `id`, `source: 'pid'` — suy đoán tốt-nhất cho terminal tay gõ (xem Open Gaps); `ps` không gọi được ngay ở tầng đầu → `id` lui về pid của chính người gọi, `source: 'unresolved'` thay vì treo/ném lỗi (`unresolved` là nhãn xuất xứ, không phải danh tính vắng mặt — giá trị `id` không đổi, per str46-io-contract). Manifest layer: kernel.
- `.githooks/pre-commit` (STR65) — hook git-native (không phải verb fgOS, không phải cấu hình riêng công cụ trợ lý nào — xem "Khóa hoạt động cây chính" trên cho hợp đồng đầy đủ): giải thư mục gốc worktree bằng `path.resolve(__dirname, '..')` (KHÔNG gọi `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` — biến môi trường `GIT_DIR` mà git tự đặt khi hook chạy TRONG một git worktree làm lời gọi đó trả sai thư mục gốc, xác nhận thật bằng tái tạo có chủ đích trước khi vá); sau các guard `.fgos`/root-file/nhánh `fgw/*`, hỏi khóa `main-checkout` MỘT lần (không chờ — git đã giữ `index.lock` khi hook chạy): hook là borrower chỉ khi đủ ba điều qua `fgos internal lock-fd --protocol 1 --borrowed-check` (`FGOS_LOCK_FD` chỉ đúng slot của `main-checkout`, `dev:ino` của slot trùng file khóa, `flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` trên slot thành công) → commit của fgOS, bỏ qua đèn; không đủ → hook thử khóa một lần bằng description riêng, đang bị giữ thì từ chối, không bao giờ xưng borrower. Rồi `resolveWriterIdentity()` và đèn hoạt động `src/runner/main-checkout-activity.mjs` (`.fgos/runtime/main-checkout-activity.json`): writer khác trong `windowMs` → từ chối; còn lại ghi đèn cuối hook với `windowMs` = `HOOK_TTL_MS` 20 s (đè được qua `FGOS_MAIN_CHECKOUT_LOCK_TTL_MS`); từ chối → in thông điệp bằng thời gian + trỏ `docs/how-to-parallel-lanes.md`, thoát khác 0.
- `scripts/install-git-hooks.mjs` (STR65) — wire `core.hooksPath` về `.githooks` khi checkout có git thật (dev clone); vắng git (cài như dependency qua `npm install <github-url>`, không giữ lại git — xem `docs/specs/distribution.md`) thì thoát 0 im lặng, không throw; gọi qua `prepare` lifecycle script của `package.json` — chạy tự động sau `npm install` trên một clone mới, không cần bước cài tay riêng.

real-fake-executor) + `test/e2e/runner-loop.test.mjs` (executor giả, repo git tạm, bao gồm 3 kịch bản stage-discovery — dispatch worker thật rồi phán quyết đủ rõ đẩy item sang `planning`, phán quyết chưa đủ rõ đẩy sang `exploring` + đậu chờ người, worker sập thì item đứng yên tại `discovery`/`todo` — cộng các kịch bản stage-clarify/stage-decompose còn lại, nay khẳng định `--once` KHÔNG tự phán ở hai tên stage đó: pass-through, chia-con-chặn-frontier, cần-người + 1 kịch bản S2-pull: `take` người + `fgos-runner --once` song song không giẫm + `return` xanh + kịch bản con fork từ tip nhánh gốc) + resolvedPassage.sample: - `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` — CLI (--once/--dry-run/--watch/--poll-ms — str7-str8-priority-intent; `--config` bỏ ở RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit
resolvedPassage.text:
- `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` — CLI (--once/--dry-run/--watch/--poll-ms — str7-str8-priority-intent; `--config` bỏ ở RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each)), exit theo phạm trù; nhánh `--watch` đăng ký `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` lên một `AbortController` chung TRƯỚC khi gọi `runWatch`, tín hiệu thứ hai buộc `process.exit(130)`; hàm `printResult` (dùng chung giữa `--once` và `onCycle` của `--watch`) nay bọc `result` (trừ `exitCode`) qua `wrapEnvelope` (`src/state/envelope.mjs`, cùng hàm `bin/fgos.mjs` dùng) và in JSON một dòng — không `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` như `fgos.mjs` — vì `--watch` phát nhiều phong bì nối tiếp theo thời gian (per str46-io-contract, xem RUL61 (kết-cục cuối của `fgos-runner` nay bọc cùng phong bì máy-đọc `fgos.v1` như mọi verb)); exit-code prose ở đầu file trỏ về `src/state/store.mjs`'s `EXIT_CODES` + `src/runner/loop.mjs`'s `EXIT_BUSY` thay vì tự liệt lại bảng
- `src/runner/loop.mjs` — vòng + startup reap (SKIP claim `human`/`session` — xem "Gặt-lại lúc khởi động") + khoá liên-tiến-trình `.fgos/locks/runner.lock` (kernel lease qua holder-lock; busy exit 6, nêu pid holder do kernel liệt kê); NGAY SAU reap, TRƯỚC vòng dispatch: (1) quét mọi item `stage==='discovery' && status==='todo'` (không đọc `item.mode`), dựng worktree tạm + `spawnWorker` với `stage: 'discovery'` cho từng item, đọc khối phán quyết trong output của worker rồi gọi `resolveDiscovery` (`src/intake/discovery.mjs`) với chính verdict đó, truyền `'runner'` — nhánh không có commit nào, hoặc không đọc được verdict, thì item được để nguyên tại chỗ cho lượt sau; (2) đọc lại view tươi rồi quét mọi item ở `stageForStep(domain,'Divide')` (`planning`) CỘNG tên di sản `decompose`, với `status==='todo'`, và gọi `resolvePlan` (`src/intake/plan.mjs`) cho từng item, cùng truyền `'runner'` — không kèm verdict, nên nó chỉ cho đi thẳng khi `plan.md` của item khai mode `tiny`/`small`, còn lại no-op an toàn; cùng lượt chạy có thể chaining cả hai sweep trên một item vừa rời `discovery`; ghi bản outcome dự đoán tại claim + thực tế ở cả hai lối ra cuối (thành đề xuất, hoặc đỗ/dừng) qua `addOutcome` của store; mọi `moveWork` runner tự gọi (claim/propose/park) truyền `role:'runner'`; gọi `runGoalCheck` (từ `goal-check.mjs`, không còn tự triển khai) cho cả proof lúc dispatch lẫn proof lúc gặt-lại; ngay trước khi spawn worker, đọc lại view TƯƠI qua `listWork(dir)` rồi truyền `feedback: {answer: view.gates?.[item.id]?.answer, reason: view.work?.[item.id]?.reason}` vào `spawnWorker` (per worker-execution STR33 / 396d9d9e, xem RUL23 (phản hồi người threading vào prompt worker)); `dispatch.mjs` — prompt/config/spawn (argv-only, spawnSync timeout; caveat grandchild SIGTERM ghi trong doc comment) + `resolveExecutorCommand`/`resolveTierModel` (dùng chung cho mọi lượt spawn worker, kể cả lượt dispatch nghiên-cứu — không còn call site nào cho một lời gọi model phán lồng bên trong engine); `buildPrompt(work, feedback?)` dựng 5 section cố định (Goal, Description, Worktree boundary, Expected proof, Constraints — hợp đồng test pin presence) cộng mục `# Human feedback` TÙY CHỌN khi `feedback.answer`/`feedback.reason` có mặt (nguyên văn, xem RUL23 (phản hồi người threading vào prompt worker)); `description` là `work.description` nguyên văn, degrade "(không có)" khi vắng (per discovery-context STR30); `spawnWorker(work, cfg, cwd, opts)` nhận `opts.feedback` truyền xuống `buildPrompt`; `worktree.mjs` — lifecycle + reclaimOrphanedCheckout + `detectTrunk(repoRoot)`/`isMainWorktree(repoRoot)` (dời từ `merge.mjs` sang đây per tsk-49i — cả hai là danh tính worktree/nhánh, không mang ngữ nghĩa nội dung merge; dời đi cũng cắt luôn import vòng `merge.mjs` ↔ `worktree.mjs`) + `createBranchRef(repoRoot, id, opts)` (tạo `fgw/<id>` chỉ-là-ref, không worktree, idempotent) + `createWorktree`'s `opts.baseRef` (fork worktree mới từ một ref chỉ định thay vì HEAD hiện tại — dùng cho con fork từ tip nhánh gốc); `recovery.mjs` — 8 lớp; `anti-loop.mjs` — `visitCount` (lifetime, dùng cho outcome/metric) + `visitsSinceLastHumanEvent(events, id)` (ngân sách CỔNG, per-item, reset trên `role==='human'` mang `answer` hoặc `reason`, xem RUL29 (cổng chống-lặp reset theo can thiệp người cuối cùng của chính việc)) + breaker; `loop.mjs`'s gate (cả nhánh dry-run đơn lẻ lẫn nhánh lọc `overLimit` của batch dispatch dưới) gọi `visitsSinceLastHumanEvent`, không còn `visitCount`, để quyết park; `createMissBreaker` nay PER-ITEM (Map theo id, `consecutiveMissesFor(itemId)`; `consecutiveMisses` getter cũ giữ nguyên qua một khóa sentinel tương thích ngược, per fan-out-parallel-5). `runOnce`'s vòng dispatch nay là pool-loop batch (cell fan-out-parallel-8): đọc TOÀN BỘ `readyWork(dir)`, lọc qua `root-affinity.mjs`'s `steerFrontier`, nhóm theo gốc và cắt còn tối đa `parallel.maxRoots × parallel.maxLeavesPerRoot` (đọc từ `.fgos/config.json`'s `runner` section, mặc định 4×4 khi vắng khối `parallel`), claim từng việc bên trong callback của `write-queue.mjs`'s `enqueue` (bắt buộc — giải-và-ghi phải cùng một giao dịch hàng đợi để giữ đúng chứng minh chống-tranh-giành), rồi dispatch cả mẻ đồng thời qua `Promise.allSettled`; mỗi việc claim xong xác định LEAF hay ROOT qua `state/frontier.mjs`'s `resolveRoot(view, id)` — leaf: `createBranchRef(repoRoot, rootId, {baseRef:'main'})` rồi `createWorktree(repoRoot, item.id, {worktreeDir, baseRef: branchNameFor(rootId)})`; root: `createWorktree` không đổi, tự nhiên tái dùng nhánh đã có nếu tồn tại. Mẻ xong → đọc lại `readyWork` tươi, lặp tới khi không còn việc đang chạy VÀ không còn việc sẵn-sàng; `runOnce` trả `{outcome, dispatched, parked, reap, exitCode}` thay vì kết quả một item
- `src/runner/loop.mjs`'s `parseDiscoveredBlocks(output)` + `captureDiscoveredWork(...)` — kênh báo việc-phát-hiện (xem "Báo việc-phát-hiện từ trợ lý" trên, RUL45 (báo việc-phát-hiện của trợ lý: đúng một lần mỗi lượt, fail-safe, có trần + chống trùng)): tách mọi khối lồng `fgos-discovered` (JSON, chỉ cần `title` khác rỗng) khỏi output đã thu của trợ lý, fail-safe (thân JSON hỏng/thiếu `title`/không phải object đều bị bỏ qua, không throw); gọi đúng MỘT LẦN trong `finally` bọc vòng thử lại của `dispatchClaimedItem`, tại kết cục cuối (không gọi lại giữa các lần thử nội bộ); mỗi khối hợp lệ đi qua `write-queue.mjs`'s `enqueue` (cùng cửa ghi tuần tự) — bên trong đó: cắt còn tối đa `DISCOVERY_CAP` (=20) khối trước khi lặp (phần dư log rồi bỏ), rồi với mỗi khối: quét view hiện hành tìm item có `discoveredFrom` khớp item đang thi công VÀ tên khớp sau khi chuẩn hoá (trim + hạ chữ) — khớp thì log rồi bỏ qua (không tạo); không khớp mới gọi `generateId`/`classify`/`addWork` (đóng dấu `discoveredFrom: item.id`, và stage vào-vòng của domain — `discovery` cho `coding`); `dispatch.mjs`'s văn bản prompt worker mô tả kênh khối lồng này cho trợ lý (nguyên tắc "chỉ báo, không tự ghi" — trợ lý vẫn không bao giờ được gọi `fgos`/đụng `.fgos/`); `sanitizeTitleForLog(title)` (S11, review-fix P3) — gộp khoảng trắng/xuống dòng + cắt 120 ký tự (kèm dấu `…` khi cắt), gọi tại đúng hai điểm `log` có nội suy `block.title` bên trong `captureDiscoveredWork`; KHÔNG áp dụng lên trường `title` truyền vào `addWork`
- `src/runner/goal-check.mjs` — hàm goal-check dùng chung DUY NHẤT (`runGoalCheck(item, cwd, timeoutMs)`): chạy `item.verify` qua shell tại `cwd`, phán chỉ bằng exit status — trích xuất từ `loop.mjs` (stage-decompose S2-pull) để cả vòng tự hành LẪN cửa pull `fgos return` (spec Work-State) gọi đúng một bản logic, không bao giờ hai bản song song
- `src/runner/frozen-judge.mjs` (STR63, domain layer thuần — không fs/git) — `FROZEN_JUDGE_PATTERNS` (bê nguyên từ frozen-judge của bee, bỏ mục `.bee/config.json` không áp dụng) + `frozenJudgeHits(changedFiles, footprint)`: chấm file đã đổi khớp nhóm nhạy cảm (test/CI/lockfile/manifest) NGOÀI `footprint` đã khai — khớp exact-path, không prefix/glob. `bin/fgos.mjs`'s `changedFilesSince(cwd, from, to)` (`git diff --name-only`, cạnh `commitsSince`) cấp input; gọi trong `return` khi `check.passed`, xem RUL60 (`return` mang thêm khuyến nghị frozen-judge — advisory, không bao giờ chặn)
- `src/intake/discovery.mjs` — xem Pointers spec Work-State (module dùng chung giữa runner và verb `discover`); verb `discover` (phiên sống) truyền `'session'`; verdict đủ rõ `moveStage` tới `planning` (bỏ qua `exploring`), verdict chưa đủ rõ `moveStage` tới `exploring` RỒI đậu `awaiting-human` mang câu hỏi (hai cửa ghi rời nhau — `stage` và `status` không giẫm nhau); một đề xuất `verify` còn phải qua một vòng kiểm cú pháp độc lập trước khi được ghi, bất đồng thì cũng đậu chờ người. `judgeDiscovery` (lời gọi phán lồng cũ) đã NGHỈ HƯU: engine luôn cần một verdict do người gọi đưa vào — worker của quét nghiên-cứu, hay phiên sống gọi `fgos discover --verdict` — thiếu verdict thì role `runner` no-op an toàn, role khác báo lỗi rõ ràng
- `src/intake/plan.mjs` (đổi tên từ `decompose.mjs`) — xem Pointers spec Work-State (module dùng chung giữa runner và verb `plan` khi item ở stage `planning`, hoặc còn ở tên di sản `decompose`); verb `plan` (phiên sống) truyền `'session'`; `resolvePlan` cũng là chỗ nhả claim `doing→todo` khi gốc sang `executing` (claim-lock §3b)
- `src/runner/prompt-templates/worker-prompt-discovery.txt` — mẫu prompt riêng của lượt dispatch nghiên-cứu, chọn bởi luật `{domain:'coding', stage:'discovery'}` trong `selectTemplate` (`src/runner/prompt-templates.mjs`); mọi lời gọi không truyền `stage` giữ nguyên hành vi cũ, không bị luật này chen trước.
